### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fb96e2ac52cb1eaf1d74b29e5247f81fca7e7664` — the merge of head `3bb9e346ac32eeb02347cbe5c0453726bd39a053` into base `e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fb96e2ac52cb1eaf1d74b29e5247f81fca7e7664 && git checkout fb96e2ac52cb1eaf1d74b29e5247f81fca7e7664
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 3bb9e346ac32eeb02347cbe5c0453726bd39a053 && git checkout -B drift-repro e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 && git merge --no-ff 3bb9e346ac32eeb02347cbe5c0453726bd39a053

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A5 · Part of #33527 (items 1 and 3) · head `3bb9e346ac32eeb02347cbe5c0453726bd39a053` · Clause-② no. CI on this head: 35 success, 16 skipped, none failing.

This is the measured follow-up card that my #33448 review ruled should follow (Q1 there).

**What was checked** (read-only: the diff, the card and the #33448 seam it extends):

- **Same seam, same rule.** Both doors call `announcePackageReload` with `{ changed: ['app/ID'] }`, the spelling of the install, enable and install-local doors. A failed announce is caught, logged once at `warn` and never changes the answer. The warn text now has a withdrawal variant that names the right consequence: flows stay armed and keep running. Case 5 pins both doors answering 200 with one warn each.
- **Disable** reads `isPackageDisabled` before `disablePackage`, the enable door's reading mirrored, and announces only when the package was enabled. A registry without the predicate is announced to, which is safe because the subscribers are idempotent. Case 1 pins that the subscriber hears the package still held and switched off. Case 2 pins that a repeated disable announces nothing.
- **DELETE** announces only when `registryRemoved`. It does so after the registry's uninstall and the verb's cleanups and before the 200 or partial-400 answer, so a subscriber re-reads a registry that no longer has the package before the caller is told. Case 3 pins `held: false` at the moment of hearing. Case 4 pins the 404 path announcing nothing.
- The ablation reds 3 of the 5 cases, and the two no-announce cases stay green in both legs, as they should.
- The jsdoc now also states that an install landing disabled is announced and harmless. That closes my #33448 N2.

**Semver:** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right. No route answer, status or export moves; two doors now raise an existing event. `@objectstack/runtime` at `patch`. `Part of` (not `Fixes`) is right, since #33527 has items beyond 1 and 3.

**Nits (none blocking):**

- **N1:** the changeset's headline ("withdraws its flows at once") rests on the automation subscriber's re-sync unregistering flows the protocol no longer lists. These pins prove the announce and its timing, not the withdrawal itself. The before-probe measured the bound flow on a real automation kernel; one after-case on that same kernel (disable, write a matching record, assert the flow did not run) would pin the headline end to end. That case can go to the #33527 remainder.

Nits only, so this is the final round. If this lands after A5's handover, the next A5 session lands it.
